title: Beshalach: stop praying, move (Exodus 14:15)
hook: at the sea, God asks Moses why he cries out, and tells the people to go forward

segments.voice: Yesterday Moses carried Joseph's bones out of Egypt while others carried silver. Your line was carry the bones. Today, the sea in front of them, and an army behind.

An email drafted and never sent. A doctor's appointment someone keeps meaning to book. A thing gets worried about, maybe prayed about, until the thinking itself becomes a place to hide. Now the Israelites are trapped: the sea ahead, Pharaoh's chariots coming up behind. The people cry out in terror. Moses tells them to stand still and watch. And then God says something to Moses that sounds, at first, almost like a rebuke.
screen: `THE EMAIL YOU NEVER SEND.` → `SEA IN FRONT, CHARIOTS BEHIND.` → `GOD SPEAKS TO MOSES.`

segments.voice: God asks Moses why he is crying out. Then: "speak unto the children of Israel, that they go forward." Here's the strange part. The Torah never shows Moses crying out. The people cried out, a few verses earlier, and Moses told them to be calm. So what is God answering? Rashi, the medieval commentator, says Moses was standing and praying silently, and God's reply means: this is not the time for long prayer; Israel is in danger. Move. Prayer isn't wrong. Moses prayed many times, and God listened. But prayer has a time, and so does walking. The rabbis also tell who took the first step. In the Talmud, Rabbi Judah says the tribes stood at the shore, each wanting someone else to go first. Then Nachshon, son of Amminadav, of the tribe of Judah, jumped into the water. In some tellings he waded in up to his neck, and only then did the sea split. That's midrash, a story the tradition tells about the gap between one verse and the next. The Torah itself simply says Moses lifted his rod, stretched his hand over the sea, and a strong east wind blew all night. The story keeps being told for the picture it leaves: the sea parting in front of someone already walking.
screen: `WHY DO YOU CRY OUT TO ME?` · `RASHI: NOT THE TIME FOR LONG PRAYER.` · `NACHSHON STEPS IN FIRST.` · `THE STRONG EAST WIND.` · then, large: `PRAY, THEN GO FORWARD.`

segments.voice: Think of one thing you've been circling. If you pray, pray about it now, briefly and honestly; if not, just name it clearly. Then picture only the first step, not the whole crossing: the first sentence of the email, the number dialed, the shoes put on, your foot touching the water.
Beshalach. When he let go. Our portion, where at the edge of the sea God tells Moses: speak to the people, and let them go forward.
Your line: pray, then go forward. Both have their time. That's day three hundred forty.

howItsDone: The crossing of the sea is read in synagogue twice a year: in the weekly portion Beshalach, and on the seventh day of Passover, which tradition dates to the night of the crossing. Nachshon is taught to children as the one who stepped in first.
